evidence.reference_title: Autosomal-dominant congenital cataract associated with a deletion mutation in the human beaded filament protein gene BFSP2.
evidence.snippet: By sequencing the coding regions of BFSP2, we found that a deletion mutation, DeltaE233, is associated with cataracts in this family.

evidence.reference_title: A juvenile-onset, progressive cataract locus on chromosome 3q21-q22 is associated with a missense mutation in the beaded filament structural protein-2.
evidence.snippet: We predicted that this led to a nonconservative R287W substitution in exon 4 that cosegregated with cataracts.

evidence.reference_title: A juvenile-onset, progressive cataract locus on chromosome 3q21-q22 is associated with a missense mutation in the beaded filament structural protein-2.
evidence.snippet: This individual's symptoms suggest that this mutation is not fully penetrant or that the age-at-onset spectrum in this family is quite broad.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical description and genome wide linkage study of Y-sutural cataract and myopia in a Chinese family.
evidence.snippet: Sequence analysis of the beaded filament structural protein 2 (BFSP2) gene identified a previously described c.697_699delGAA (E233del) mutation which was present in all individuals with Y-sutural cataract but not in unaffected individuals and controls.

evidence.reference_title: A new mutation in BFSP2 (G1091A) causes autosomal dominant congenital lamellar cataracts.
evidence.snippet: Sequencing the beaded filament structural protein 2 (BFSP2) gene revealed a G>A transversion in exon 5, which caused a conservative substitution of Arg to His at codon 339 (P.R339H).

evidence.reference_title: A novel p.G112E mutation in BFSP2 associated with autosomal dominant pulverulent cataract with sutural opacities.
evidence.snippet: Direct candidate gene sequencing revealed a heterozygous c. 335 G>A variation in the beaded filament structural protein 2(BFSP2) gene, which resulted in the replacement of a highly conserved glycine by glutamic at codon 112 (p. G112E).

evidence.reference_title: Identification of mutations associated with congenital cataracts in nineteen Chinese families.
evidence.snippet: The variant BFSP2: exon3: c.697_699del in family 4 was classified as LP and has been reported to segregate with disease in multiple affected family members

evidence.reference_title: Pathogenic genetic variants identified in Australian families with paediatric cataract.
evidence.snippet: In family CQLD130, the BFSP2 p.(Arg89Trp) variant was observed in four affected individuals and a child who was unaffected as the 10 years old at last examination, but not yet old enough to be confirmed as unaffected for a childhood onset disease

nodes.description: Phakinin and filensin cannot form filaments alone and co-assemble into the beaded filament. Without CP49, filensin protein falls although its mRNA is unchanged, and no beaded filaments form in fiber cells.

animal_models.description: CP49 protein is absent and filensin protein is reduced, so no beaded filaments form.

animal_models.description: The strains lack CP49 and beaded filaments and behave as functional CP49 knockouts.

evidence.reference_title: Functions of the intermediate filament cytoskeleton in the eye lens.
evidence.snippet: Neither BFSP1 nor BFSP2 appear capable of assembling alone into IFs in vitro

evidence.reference_title: Seeing is believing! The optical properties of the eye lens are dependent upon a functional intermediate filament cytoskeleton.
evidence.snippet: Whilst CP49 is completely tailless, filensin has a rather short rod domain and extremely large C-terminal tail domain. In vitro, CP49 and filensin do not form IFs on their own.

evidence.reference_title: Targeted genomic deletion of the lens-specific intermediate filament protein CP49.
evidence.snippet: Filensin levels were sharply reduced, although filensin mRNA levels appeared unchanged.

evidence.reference_title: Bfsp2 mutation found in mouse 129 strains causes the loss of CP49 and induces vimentin-dependent changes in the lens fibre cell cytoskeleton.
evidence.snippet: Electron microscopy of the lens cytoskeleton from 129S2/SvPas revealed similar morphological changes in the cytoskeleton as compared to the CP49 knockout, with beaded and intermediate filaments being apparently replaced by poorly defined filament-like material.

nodes.description: The recessive allele in the Saudi family is described as likely null. Targeted or natural Bfsp2 null alleles in mice abolish CP49 protein and the beaded filament, which is the closest model for this genotype.

evidence.reference_title: Novel recessive BFSP2 and PITX3 mutations: insights into mutational mechanisms from consanguineous populations.
evidence.snippet: In one family, a novel BFSP2 mutation causes autosomal recessive diffuse cortical cataract with scattered lens opacities

nodes.description: Lens extraction, with intraocular lens implantation where appropriate, is the treatment for visually significant opacity; affected members of BFSP2 families have had surgery from early childhood to age 50. No BFSP2-specific therapy exists.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal-dominant congenital cataract associated with a deletion mutation in the human beaded filament protein gene BFSP2.
evidence.snippet: The acuity declined to 20/50 in the right eye; cataract surgery with intraocular lens implantation restored the acuity to 20/25.

evidence.reference_title: A juvenile-onset, progressive cataract locus on chromosome 3q21-q22 is associated with a missense mutation in the beaded filament structural protein-2.
evidence.snippet: The ages for cataract surgery were 12–50 years.

evidence.reference_title: Updates on managements of pediatric cataract.
evidence.snippet: This review article suggests that lens opacity obscuring the red reflex in preverbal children and visual acuity of less than 20/40 is an absolute indication for lens aspiration.

nodes.description: Spokelike anterior and posterior subcapsular cortical opacities with fine radial vacuoles in the mildest dominant E233del cases; diffuse cortical cataract with scattered or fleck-like opacities in the recessive family.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal-dominant congenital cataract associated with a deletion mutation in the human beaded filament protein gene BFSP2.
evidence.snippet: The mildest expression of the cataract was that of spokelike anterior and posterior subcapsular cortical opacities with a ground-glass appearance throughout the cataract and, most notably, the radially oriented fine vacuoles

evidence.reference_title: Novel recessive BFSP2 and PITX3 mutations: insights into mutational mechanisms from consanguineous populations.
evidence.snippet: In one family, a novel BFSP2 mutation causes autosomal recessive diffuse cortical cataract with scattered lens opacities

evidence.reference_title: Phenotypes of Recessive Pediatric Cataract in a Cohort of Children with Identified Homozygous Gene Mutations (An American Ophthalmological Society Thesis).
evidence.snippet: EPHA2 (bilateral anterior persistent fetal vasculature), and BFSP2 (bilateral flecklike with cloudy cortex)

nodes.description: Cataract present at birth or in early childhood in most dominant families, including total cataract at birth in an E233del family.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal-dominant congenital cataract associated with a deletion mutation in the human beaded filament protein gene BFSP2.
evidence.snippet: Affected members of the family had congenital nuclear, sutural, and stellate or spokelike cortical cataracts that varied in severity among different individuals.

evidence.reference_title: A new mutation in BFSP2 (G1091A) causes autosomal dominant congenital lamellar cataracts.
evidence.snippet: The proband was a six-year-old female (IV:25) who had bilateral cataracts since birth.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and genetic characteristics of Chinese patients with familial or sporadic pediatric cataract.
evidence.snippet: An in-frame deletion c.697_699del; p.(Glu233del) in the intermediate filament rod domain of BFSP2, previously reported by Jakobs PM and Zhang Q ... was identified in all affected individuals of family #11 with total cataract

nodes.description: Dominant alleles cluster in the alpha-helical central rod domain, which mediates coiled-coil dimerization: R287W, the recurrent in-frame E233del and R339H; G112E lies near the head-rod boundary. E233 and R287 are conserved across species and among intermediate filament proteins, and deleting E233 is predicted to shift the heptad repeat phase. Because a likely null allele causes no cataract in heterozygous carriers, the dominant alleles are thought to act by a mechanism other than haploinsufficiency; no functional study of a human BFSP2 allele was found.

evidence.reference_title: A juvenile-onset, progressive cataract locus on chromosome 3q21-q22 is associated with a missense mutation in the beaded filament structural protein-2.
evidence.snippet: This mutation alters an evolutionarily conserved arginine residue in the central rod domain of the intermediate filament.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal-dominant congenital cataract associated with a deletion mutation in the human beaded filament protein gene BFSP2.
evidence.snippet: Deletion of residue E233 would result in a phase shift in the 1,4 periodicity and would perturb an otherwise highly conserved property among IF proteins.

evidence.reference_title: Novel recessive BFSP2 and PITX3 mutations: insights into mutational mechanisms from consanguineous populations.
evidence.snippet: The likely null nature of both mutations and lack of manifestation in heterozygotes strongly argues for a mechanism other than loss of function in the previously reported dominant mutations in these two genes.

nodes.description: In the R287W family the lens was clear at birth and opacity was first documented between age 8 and the late 20s, without nystagmus or impaired visual development; surgery was done between 12 and 50 years.

evidence.reference_title: A juvenile-onset, progressive cataract locus on chromosome 3q21-q22 is associated with a missense mutation in the beaded filament structural protein-2.
evidence.snippet: No individuals were diagnosed with cataracts at birth, nor did any individuals have nystagmus or impaired visual development as a result of the lens opacities.

evidence.reference_title: A juvenile-onset, progressive cataract locus on chromosome 3q21-q22 is associated with a missense mutation in the beaded filament structural protein-2.
evidence.snippet: Family members ranged in age at onset from 9 years to late 20s.

nodes.description: Lamellar opacity in advanced cases of the juvenile R287W family and from birth in the R339H family.

evidence.reference_title: A juvenile-onset, progressive cataract locus on chromosome 3q21-q22 is associated with a missense mutation in the beaded filament structural protein-2.
evidence.snippet: The earliest reported findings were a general haze of the lens with prominent sutures, and all of the individuals with more advanced cases demonstrated lamellar cataracts without discrete subcapsular or nuclear opacities.

evidence.reference_title: A new mutation in BFSP2 (G1091A) causes autosomal dominant congenital lamellar cataracts.
evidence.snippet: This four-generation family included 17 affected individuals with congenital lamellar cataracts and 56 unaffected individuals (Figure 2).

nodes.description: CP49-null mouse lenses are clear at birth and develop slowly progressive light scattering and loss of optical quality; one knockout line was judged not to form a frank cataract. In patients this corresponds to congenital, juvenile or progressive lens opacity of variable morphology.

evidence.reference_title: Targeted genomic deletion of the lens-specific intermediate filament protein CP49.
evidence.snippet: The absence of CP49 causes a subtle loss of optical clarity in the ocular lens, a loss that worsens with age.

evidence.reference_title: Knockout of the intermediate filament protein CP49 destabilises the lens fibre cell cytoskeleton and decreases lens optical quality, but does not induce cataract.
evidence.snippet: Light scatter and the lens optical properties had, however, deteriorated in the CP49 knockout lenses compared to litter mate controls.

evidence.reference_title: Functions of the intermediate filament cytoskeleton in the eye lens.
evidence.snippet: The progressive nature of the increased light scatter and cataract development for the mouse Bfsp1 and Bfsp2 knockouts (52, 74) and the human cataracts caused by BFSP1 (56) and BFSP2 (49, 53, 54) mutations suggest that there is an aging element to the beaded filament contribution to the optical properties of the lens.

nodes.description: In CP49-null lenses fiber cells differentiate and elongate normally, then lose their shape, membrane organization and long-range stacking as they mature. The lenses are also smaller and less stiff than wild type. The Y-shaped sutural opacity of E233del families is thought to reflect a change in the internal cellular organization of the lens.
nodes.id: Loss of Fiber Cell Architecture and Long-Range Order

evidence.reference_title: Resisting the effects of aging: a function for the fiber cell beaded filament.
evidence.snippet: In phakosin and filensin knockout mice, initial lens development and the early phases of fiber cell differentiation proceed in a manner largely indistinguishable from that of wild type.

evidence.reference_title: Resisting the effects of aging: a function for the fiber cell beaded filament.
evidence.snippet: Subsequent to those stages, however, fiber cells undergo loss of the differentiated fiber cell phenotype and loss of the long-range stacking that characterizes fiber cells and that has been considered essential for clarity.

evidence.reference_title: Knockout of the intermediate filament protein CP49 destabilises the lens fibre cell cytoskeleton and decreases lens optical quality, but does not induce cataract.
evidence.snippet: These changes were accompanied by dramatic changes in plasma membrane organisation of the fibre cells as revealed by detailed morphological examinations

evidence.reference_title: Intermediate filaments regulate tissue size and stiffness in the murine lens.
evidence.snippet: The absence of these filaments resulted in lenses that were smaller, and exhibited a higher ratio of lens:lens nucleus size.

evidence.reference_title: Functions of the intermediate filament cytoskeleton in the eye lens.
evidence.snippet: The Y-shaped cataract for the E233del mutation in BFSP2 (Figure 5) has its origins in changes to the internal cellular organization of the lens (Figure 1).

nodes.description: Myopia was found in 10 of 12 affected members of one Y-sutural E233del family and was mild; it has not been reported in other BFSP2 families, and the myopia locus was mapped to a broad interval around BFSP2, so whether BFSP2 causes it is unresolved.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical description and genome wide linkage study of Y-sutural cataract and myopia in a Chinese family.
evidence.snippet: Myopia, observed in 10 out of 12 cataract patients and significantly higher than that in unaffected offspring and siblings (1 out of 8), was independently mapped to a 61.2 cM (59 Mb) region between D3S3606 and D3S1262 on 3q21.3-q27.2 with maximum lod score of 3.79.

evidence.reference_title: Functions of the intermediate filament cytoskeleton in the eye lens.
evidence.snippet: Only one of the three E233del BFSP2 pedigrees has been reported to exhibit myopia, albeit mild (53), and in that family pedigree, there was no evidence supporting the idea that myopia was caused by changes in lens morphology.

nodes.description: Congenital nuclear opacity, including pulverulent opacity in the embryonal nucleus.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal-dominant congenital cataract associated with a deletion mutation in the human beaded filament protein gene BFSP2.
evidence.snippet: Affected members of the family had congenital nuclear, sutural, and stellate or spokelike cortical cataracts that varied in severity among different individuals.

evidence.reference_title: A novel p.G112E mutation in BFSP2 associated with autosomal dominant pulverulent cataract with sutural opacities.
evidence.snippet: All affected individuals presented pulverulent opacities in the embryonal nucleus and sutures.

nodes.description: Posterior polar radial cataract in one Chinese E233del family.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of mutations associated with congenital cataracts in nineteen Chinese families.
evidence.snippet: The cataract phenotype resulting from the BFSP2: c.697_699del is mostly nuclear, Y-sutural, stellate, or spokelike cortical, which is consistent with the posterior polar radial cataract reported in family 4

nodes.description: Opacity worsens over years in the R287W family and in two E233del families.

evidence.reference_title: Progressive sutural cataract associated with a BFSP2 mutation in a Chinese family.
evidence.snippet: We observed progressive isolated sutural cataract associated with a deletion mutation of the BFSP2 gene in a Chinese pedigree.

evidence.reference_title: The E233del mutation in BFSP2 causes a progressive autosomal dominant congenital cataract in a Chinese family.
evidence.snippet: The progressive phenotype has provided more evidence for the heterogeneity of congenital cataract caused by BFSP2 mutations and for the important role BFSP2 plays in cataract formation.

nodes.description: Dust-like opacities in the embryonal nucleus and sutures in the G112E family.

evidence.reference_title: A novel p.G112E mutation in BFSP2 associated with autosomal dominant pulverulent cataract with sutural opacities.
evidence.snippet: All affected individuals presented pulverulent opacities in the embryonal nucleus and sutures.

evidence.reference_title: Pathogenic genetic variants identified in Australian families with paediatric cataract.
evidence.snippet: Sutural, often pulverulent-like, cataracts are the most frequently reported phenotype with BFSP2 variants while the range of phenotypes observed for BFSP1 variants is wider and includes nuclear, lamellar and cortical cataracts.

nodes.description: Opacity along the lens sutures, typically involving the anterior Y and posterior inverted-Y sutures with a feather-duster appearance in E233del families; also prominent sutures early in the R287W family and sutural pulverulent opacity with G112E.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical description and genome wide linkage study of Y-sutural cataract and myopia in a Chinese family.
evidence.snippet: Bilateral lens opacities, the only sign of cataract in early childhood and the most prominent sign in all affected individuals, involved the entire anterior Y and posterior inverted Y sutures, showing a feather duster like appearance.

evidence.reference_title: Progressive sutural cataract associated with a BFSP2 mutation in a Chinese family.
evidence.snippet: To identify the mutation underlying the segregation of progressive sutural congenital cataracts in a four-generation Chinese pedigree.
